messages:
incident-bot: :warning: prod alert: continuous-batcher (us-east-1) high paging + increased 5xx rate. detected at 1865445000. summary: kv_cache_paging=96%, 5xx=5.8% (5m), p95_token_latency=2.1s.

sanjay: i'm taking lead. seeing a lot of cache reloads and disk page stalls in the node logs. looks like batch sizing exploded after the last deploy. dropping in the current config now.

meera: can you paste the config values? i want to confirm if MAX_NUM_SEQS or timeout got bumped.

sanjay: configmap snippet:
```yaml
data:
  MAX_BATCH_TOKENS: "999999999"
  MAX_NUM_SEQS: "2048"
  BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS: "5000"
```
those timeout and sizes will allow massive batches to sit and pressure the kvcache.

tom: yep that matches the symptoms. huge batches -> KV entries blow past memory window -> kernel paging -> tail latency spike -> request timeouts and 500s. Impacted paths: streaming textgen and chat endpoints for some enterprise tenants.

ops-bot: Alert: customer-impacted tickets created: CUS-4321, CUS-4322.

meera: mitigation proposal (fast): 1) apply emergency config patch to set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=8192, MAX_NUM_SEQS=16, BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=400 2) kill long-running pods to free cache ASAP (graceful) 3) add temporary rate cap per-tenant for heavy customers to reduce influx.

adrienne: agree, add immediate metric watch: KV_CACHE_ENTRIES, page_faults/sec, continuous-batch 5xx. i'll coordinate the tenant rate caps.

sanjay: executing patch:
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap continuous-batcher-cm --type merge -p '{"data":{"MAX_BATCH_TOKENS":"8192","MAX_NUM_SEQS":"16","BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS":"400"}}' && kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher
```
Applying patch now.

ops-bot: Patch applied by sanjay at 1865445123. Rolling restart initiated (replicas=4).

kevin: monitoring: pod-a restart ok, pod-b restart ok. after pod-b p95 dropped to 1.0s, 5xx 2.6%. after pod-c p95 0.7s. tail pod-d still draining.

support-bot: Customer ticket CUS-4321 updated: "We pushed an emergency fix; we're seeing performance improvements and will follow up."

meera: verifying kvcache size: before = 22.4M entries, after pod-c = 2.0M entries. paging pressure cleared to 12%.

adrienne: i'll run a quick blame scan on deploys to find the PR that injected the bad defaults. please hold hotfix values until postmortem. also add a temporary alert rule: KV_CACHE_ENTRIES > 10M for > 2m -> paged escalation.

sanjay: handoff: i'll hand to meera in 15m but will remain shadowing. please don't change the emergency caps until postmortem.

meera: observed stability for 12m, 5xx ~0.1%, p95 0.5s. customers report fewer errors. logging shows eviction_rate normalized.

kevin: created incident ticket INC-2026 and assigned owners: infra=adrienne, runtime=sanjay, cs=kevin. postmortem required.

adrienne: opened INFRA-4901 to add Helm value schema (min/max) and a pre-deploy sanity check that rejects MAX_NUM_SEQS > 256 or MAX_BATCH_TOKENS > 1_000_000. also adding unit tests to ensure default values are sane.

meera: follow-ups: - runbook update to include 'verify batch config after deploy' checklist - add CI gate to the deploy pipeline - notify affected customers with timeline (kevin)

sanjay: quick note for postmortem: investigate whether a recent templating change caused integer overflow or incorrect defaults in config generation. include exact commit sha and deploy id.

kevin: customer outreach queued; will post timeline + remediation steps once postmortem is ready.

ops-bot: Live mitigation closed at 1865445375. Incident severity set to SEV2.

meera: closing: exec summary draft: root cause = misconfigured continuous batching defaults pushed to prod allowing excessively large batches; effect = KV cache growth + paging leading to latency and 5xxs for a subset of customers; mitigation = emergency config patch + rolling restart + tenant rate caps; next steps = infra fixes, CI/deploy guards, runbook and customer comms.

sanjay: thanks team, great triage. tagging for postmortem INC-2026. :white_check_mark:
